(corresponds to Pali apakassati, used in same passage, see s.v.), holds back, keeps under control: ger. avakṛṣya (kāyam, cittam), Candropama Sūtra, (); see s.v. jarodapāna.

(see ava), no practice of love: (vs; wrongly divided in ed.) dvātriṃśa māsām (= māsān, acc. pl.) avakāmaseva (= ˚vā, n. sg.) hi, for she abstained from love-making for 32 months; so Tib. renders. There is a v.l. akāma for avakāma but it is metrically impossible.

(caus. to Pali avakassati, apak˚, apakāsati; cf. Skt. kas-), removes, dismisses: ˚yitavyaḥ

(= Pali okoṭ˚), deformed, misshapen; so Tib. acc. to, byad (on byed) ṅan po; the precise mg. in Pali is disputed; and, in phrase durvarṇo durdarśano ava˚; in Pali only in corresp. phrase dubbaṇṇa duddas(s)ika oko˚. (= Skt. id., in garbhāva˚,,; Pali avakkanti, okk˚), entrance; common in garbhāva˚ entrance into the womb (as in Skt.), etc.; tathāgatadivasāvakrānti-vijñapti-vyūhānāṃ (bodhisattvānāṃ), having supernal manifestations (or, a mass?) of knowledge of the coming in (? occurrence) of the day of the Tathāgata (or, the Tathāgataʼs entrance into the light of day?).

(= Pali otāra, esp. in mg. 4) [(1) as in Skt., descent, appearance (on earth), e.g. ˚raṃ gacchati, appears, is born;] (2) entrance into, attainment of (a moral state), -mahākaruṇāvatāra-tāṃ, state of attainment of great compassion; so, perhaps (or to 3), pratisaṃvid-avatāro and pratiśaraṇāvatāro, and 17; mahākaruṇāvatārābhimukhāni cittāni, thoughts tending to attainment of great compassion; (3) intellectual penetration, comprehension (cf. avatarati): and 11 and pratītyāvatāra-, penetration, comprehension of (origination by) dependence, see pratītya; ekaviṣaya-sarvadharma-samatāvatāra-cakraṃ wheel of the comprehension of the equality of all substantial states as belonging to one sphere; followed in cpd. by (-jñāna)-kuśala or -kauśalya, clever(-ness) in (the knowledge of) the penetration of … (Tib. ḥjug pa, entrance), -avatāra-kuśala; -kauśalya; -avatāra-jñāna-kuśala;; -svabhāvāvatāra(-tā); in = meter (supported by some [Page071-b] readings of mss.) indicates reading jñānasāgar'avatāra nāyakā(ḥ), the cpd. agreeing with preceding mānasaṃ, (a mind) that penetrates into the ocean of knowledge; avatāreṇa, by penetration,; yathāsvam avatāraiḥ (so read); avatārataḥ; avatāraḥ;; -sukhopāyāvatāra-dharmadeśanatā, preaching doctrines that are capable of comprehension by easy means; mahāyāna-samudayāvatāra-nirdeśanām avatarati; (4) (way of) entrance, ingress in the sense of opportunity for hostile approach; weak spot, often as object of a form of labh or adhi-gam, find, obtain, the subject often being Māra the Evil One, so (na ca tatra māraḥ pāpīyān) avatāraṃ lapsyate (om. with v.l.); esp. often in cpds. avatāra-prekṣin (cf. (not in Skt.; in Pali only pass. ovuyhati is carried off by a river,), carries, bears (a burden): -dhuram avavoḍhum (inf.).

(so regularly, otherwise ava˚; to avavadati) m. (= Pali ovāda), admonition, instruction: sattvāvavāda-kuśalānāṃ; datto 'vavādo 'bhūt, the admonition (instruction) was granted; ovādena ovadanti;;;;;;;;; bodhisattvāvavāda, et alibi, epithet of Mahāvaipulya sūtras such as (for this regularly reads bodhisattvotpāda, note to l. c.); parallel with the virtual synonym anuśāsanī, q.v., karaṇīyo ovādo karaṇīyā anuśāsanī; these two often compounded as avavādānuśāsanī (ovādānu˚), dvandva, but regularly sg. with fem. gender (): (read with mss. avavādānuśāsanī, or ˚nīm, asya; the reading of both edd. is impossible), admonition and instruction:; =;;;;;.

, adj. (to avavadati; = Pali ovādaka), instructing, admonishing; m., instructor (in religion); nt. also used of a text: yas teṣām ṛṣir avavādakaḥ; ˚kānām agro; (ko 'smākam) avavādaka ājñaptaḥ; kulāvavādako, a family (religious) instructor, of a rich man; mahāyānasyāvavādakāni (are instructors in the Mahāyāna) mama kalyāṇamitrāṇi; nt., of a work, Rājāvavādakam, see this.
= avavadati; noted only in iminā ovādena ovādito and … ovāditvā 10; prob. denom. to ovāda (ava˚).
(n. ag. to avavadati, or to prec.?), one who instructs or admonishes: ˚tāraḥ pāramitāsu.
, seeming text, but only by misprint; see gurula.]

, read avamaṃsyati, fut. of ava-manyate, with var. in Kyoto ed., and with ʼs text without v.l. No ava-śaṃs is recorded anywhere, if we except the noun avaśas, ἅπ. λεγ. Moreover no ya- present to śaṃs is known.]
(nowhere recorded), lies down: (vs) paryaṅke 'vaśayitvā (ger.). Cf. avaśāyita.
, only in ˚kha-praśākha, adj., having down-hanging twigs or branches, said of several kinds of trees: ośākha-praśākhaṃ (nyagrodhapotaṃ); ˚kho (kakubho nāma vṛkṣo); avaśākhapraśākhā (harītakī).

, ppp. (cf. avaśayati; this form could be m.c. for avaśayita), lying, resting, bedded: (vs) dārikā dārakā caiva śayyāsanāvaśāyitāḥ (; [Page075-b] mss. śayyāyām avaś˚, śayyāsanaśāyitā, the latter metrically bad).
, adv. (āmreḍita cpd.; avaśam, adv. from Skt. avaśa), quite certainly:.

(also spelled with ṣ, s for ś, and mss. sometimes show a for i after the sibilant, oṣarati, (2) osarati; see avasarati; cf. Pkt. Lex. osiraṇa = vyutsarjana, parityāga,; etym. obscure, cf., noting semantic correspondence with Skt. ava-sṛj): (1) clears away: (vs) vīthi racita ratnavastra-dhāryai(r) (˚dhānyair, grain, with Tib. ḥbrus) avaśiriyā (ger.), having cleared the streets which were adorned etc. (before the Bodhisattva); (2) sends off, throws (into prison): osiranti (see,); (3) sends forth, emits (light, sound, breath): mukhavātam (so with v.l. for ˚vāṭam) osireyā, (if the Bodhisattva) should send forth the breath of his mouth;, read prob. avaśiri sent forth (a ray of light; mss. avaśiti, avati; em. avasṛjati); (should be read) ˚sahasrāṃś c'ośarī(r) ātmabhāvā. probably (Buddha) sent forth from his body (hundreds of) thousands (of rays), see; (vs) raśmisamudra ośiratu (n. sg. m. pres. pple.); in (vs) 1st ed. eṣiriṣū jinaḥ, read osiri pūjitaḥ (see 2d ed.); osire (v.l. ośire) would send forth (svaraṃ, a sound); (4) throws down (fragrant powder, flowers; said of gods, upon the Bodhisattva or Buddha; = avakirati, which reads by em. in and): avaśire (or ˚sire, mss.) cūrṇadhārāṃ … varacandanasya; ratanacūrṇaṃ antarīkṣāto osire (v.l. ośire; here kept by); puṣpavarṣāṇi antarīkṣeṇa ośiri (mss.); also of throwing down missiles, (vs) vajrāmayaparvatā-śanī (i.e. aśanī; v.l. yadi, so, emending to ˚parvato; acc.) ghatanārthāya ca (hi) mūrdhi (better with v.l. ˚dha, loc.; ˚dhni) oṣaret, if one should hurl down on his head to kill him … (for ʼs interpretation see avasarati 1); (5) lets loose, releases: (devīm) ośiritvā (after violently seizing her); yadi me na osariṣyasi (so mss., em. osir˚) … ātmānaṃ mārayiṣyaṃ; lets go (women from a harem), gives license to: ośiritavyā (em. ˚yaṃ); (note ośiṣṭā, v.l. ośiriṣṭā,, not osṛṣṭa as quoted from this place by; text seems to intend pple. of ava-śiṣ, left alone, and so abandoned;) the subject is strīkāgāraṃ (v.l. strīyāg˚), the women of the harem must be turned loose (to carry on affairs with other men); so (istriyāgāraṃ, v.l. stryā˚) ośiritavyā (em. ˚yaṃ); striyāgāraṃ (mss.) ośirati (mss. ˚riti); in another version of the same story,, mss. osare(yaṃ) (em. osir˚), but and ośirati (stryāgāram); but on the borderline between this and the next, or belonging perhaps to the next, are (in the same story) mā hevaṃ māṃ imasya brāhmaṇasya upasthānaparicaryāye osiriṣyati (; mss. ośiri˚, osari˚), Iʼm afraid he will hand me over to serve and wait on this brahman (spoken by the chief queen); na me … eṣo brāhmaṇo ośiriṣyati, … will not give me up; (6) abandons, throws out or away, renounces (cf. the last two citations): padumāvatīṃ vadhyām avasirasi, you abandon Padumāvatī to be killed; ośiritvā kāmaratiṃ, abandoning the pleasure of desire, repeated where mss. osaritvă (ośir˚) and where mss. okiritvā (ośir˚); osirāhi (v.l. ośirehi) bhagavato traimāsaṃ bhaktam, give up (renounce, resign the right to); (vs) divya ośiritvā (so 1 ms., v.l. okiritvā, wrongly em. otaritvā) giving up heavenly things; vasudhāṃ sarvāṃ osiritvā (so 1 ms., v.l. osar˚), abandoning the whole earth; ośiritvāna (oneʼs family, to lead a religious life); suvarṇaniṣkāṃ … ośiritvā, throwing away gold coins;, mss. manuṣya-pātraṃ [Page076-a] (read madhusya p˚? amṛtasya p˚, bad metrically and otherwise) … ośiritvā viṣasya pātraṃ pibed bālabuddhiḥ.

, adj. (= Pali avasesa), left over, remaining: yaṃ teṣām asthīni avaśeṣāṇi (but so only 1 ms., the other 5 avaśeṣanti) bhūyo 'pi mānsachavi(?) … upajāyati, when (only) their bones are left, flesh and skin is produced again. See also kalpāvaśeṣam, niravaśeṣa, saṃghāvaśeṣa, sāvaśeṣa.

(m. or nt.; = AMg. osa; Skt. avaśyāya, once Lex. avaśyā, f.), hoarfrost, as symbol of transitoriness, used of life or worldly things: (vs) osavindūpamā … śūnyasvabhāvā(ḥ), like drops of hoarfrost (fleeting and vain); jīviti svapnanibhe cali 'vaśye (states that Tib. renders hoarfrost, which he unwisely abandons); (vs, cited from Candrapradīpa Sūtra =, but not the same vs) jīvite cañcale 'vaśye māyāsvapnanibhopame. In the osa could be m.c. for osā = Skt. (Lex.) avaśyā; but the loc. (a)vaśye in the others points to a m. or nt. stem; AMg. osa is given by as m.
(denom. from prec.), turns into hoarfrost: (prose) (svedāḥ …) bhūmau nipatanti sma, avaśyāyanta ūṣmāyanto …

, m., lit. frost-cloth, a fine silk fabric, allegedly ‘used for protection against frost’ () = Tib. dar-la (which also renders paṭṭāṃśu and aṃśuka): ˚paṭṭaḥ (v.l. ˚paṭaḥ: ˚paṭṭaḥ, no v.l.); (prose) avaśyāyapaṭa-vitata-vitāne.
, f. ˚tā (= Pali avassuta; cf. an-ava˚; derived from Skt. root sru, for which even Skt. texts often read śru), (sexually) lustful: bhikṣuṇī avaśrutā avaśrutena puruṣeṇa …; (see s.v. saṃcagghati).ʼ

, m., some part of a building: = Tib. ya phubs (? top roof?). informs me that the Chin. translation now means grand, huge or empty, but that the ‘radical’ of the sign suggests a possible original meaning roof. In acc. to Tib. large beam, gduṅ bo che.
, ger. (cf. s.v. stabh with ava, 4), embracing, enveloping: bhagavantaṃ bodhisattvāṃś ca ratnajālenāva˚, embracing, enclosing in a (? magic) network (? mass) of jewels.

(= Pali o-sa˚; see s.v. -sakkati), withdraws, retreats: (apy ekatyāḥ palāyanti) apy ekatyā na palāyanti apy ekatyā kutrāpi avasakkanti (mss. ˚sappanti, one ˚sarppanti) apy ekatyā na avasakkanti (so 2 mss.; others ˚sarkkanti, ˚śakyanti, ˚sappanti); so dāni vyāghro taṃ ṛṣiṃ dṛṣṭvā osakkito (no v.l. in Critical App., but indicates that mss. read osaṃkito); (vs) yadi si na maritukāmo, osakka (2 sg. impv.) mama rājyato.

, (1) osarati, once oṣar˚ (?); on forms with sār- see below, but also caus. s.v. 1 osarati (cf. Pali avasarati, osarati, to enter, to arrive,), (1) approaches, arrives: (vs) tasmiṃ narake osaranti, they arrive at this hell (otherwise); osarantasya, and ˚nto 10 (pres. pple.), approaching, drawing near; aor. avasāri or ˚riṃ, 1st or 3d sg., in phrase yena … tad avasāri(ṃ), arrived at, went to where … was (on the long ā see; the corresponding Pali phrase is tad avasari, e.g.); (in 16 mss. anusāri);;;;;; aor. with short ă, osare (mṛgābhimukhaṃ, {{approched->approached||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}}, went up in the direction of the deer, in hunting); vanāto so osare rājadhānīṃ; (= Pali), read: na te koṣṭhesmiṃ osaranti (go to, resort to; Pali upenti) na [Page076-b] kumbhe na kalopiyaṃ (see s.v. kalopī); ekaromi sugatasya osarī (3 pl. aor.), settled, lodged; osari (read) prajñapradīpa ya osari, and 15;; oṣaret (opt.), see avaśirati 4, vajrāmaya-parvato yadi ghatanārthāya hi mūrdhni oṣaret, should alight, fall upon his head, which is perhaps possible; (2) osarati and its forms also are written for ośirati (avaśirati, q.v.); in my opinion this set of forms must be wholly unrelated to the above (despite). Perhaps ośir˚ (or osir˚) should always be read by em. when osar˚ occurs in the mss. in the meanings of avaśirati. Note especially osare(yaṃ), mss. (osir˚), but in and mss. ośirati in precisely similar context.

, adj. (Skt. and Pali apasavya; Pkt. avasavvaya, cf. AMg. avasavva, a particular kind of the motions of the planets), not left, right (-hand): ˚vyaṃ; ˚vyena (adv.) on the right; utsaṅgasthitāvasavyahastaṃ.
, m. (to avasādayati), abuse: = Tib. smad pa, or spyo ba.

(to avasādayati), (1) adj., f. ˚nī, censuring, rebuking: (kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ …) saṃcodanāvasādanī priyavāditā; (2) ˚nā, subst. f. censure, rebuke: avasādanā madhyame vyatikrame, censure (is appropriate) in case of a transgression (of) middling (gravity);, see s.v. avasādayati; avasādanāsādhyaḥ, to be perfected by censure; tām avasādanām amṛṣyamāṇaḥ, impatient of this rebuke; avasādanāvineyaḥ, to be converted (substantially = ˚nā-sādhyaḥ, above) by rebuke (which is applied in 7 in the words tvaṃ tāvac cūḍaḥ etc.; ed. Index discouragement, not quite rightly; the opposite is utsahanā-vineya, see utsahanā); in (saṃcārya) vicāryāvasādanākāreṇa pāṇiṃ saṃcārayati sma (subject, the Bodhisattva in his motherʼs womb);, ‘en lʼétendant pour le signal du départ’ (sc. for the attendant gods), but avasādanā can hardly mean this. Tib. had a quite different reading, containing smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan as in (dran zhiṅ śes bzhin du, both times). I cannot solve the passage but think it probably corrupt, despite the lack of variants. Perhaps follow the lead of Tib.
, censure, rebuke:, see prec. and s.v. avasādayati; similarly.

(= Pali apasādayati, in both mgs.; cf. prec. two), (1) rejects, repulses: tāye māṇavikāye … avasādito, rejected by this girl (with whom he was in love); (2) censures, rebukes: (mṛdvaparādhaṃ mṛdu-vyatikramaṃ …) mṛdvyā (text mṛdhvyā) avasādanikayā avasādayati; so also; toṣayatā utsāhayatā anavasādayatā, by him gratifying, enthusing, not reproaching; bodhisattvaḥ avasādanārhān … pravāsanārhān kliṣṭacitto nāvasādayati, avasādayati vā na ca daṇḍakarmanā samanuśāsti; ˚yitavyaḥ.
, nt. (seemingly = osāraṇā, q.v.), restitution (of a monk that has been suspended from the order): ˚ṇam = Tib. bzod par gsol ba, request for forgiveness; so also Chin.
, nt. (to Skt. avasṛjati), emission, pouring forth: (prose) bodhisattvanirmitameghāvasṛjanaṃ.
(no ava-sev is recorded), having cultivated, devoted oneself to: pañcavidhapuṇyakriyāvastv-avasevitavatas (bodhisattvasya); Calc. reads upasev˚ for avasev˚, unsupported by any of ʼs mss.

(cf. Skt. avaskandana, nt., accusation, legal attack; to ava-skand-, attack, usually in military sense), (verbal) attack; injurious speech; ˚skandanā is read for ˚sphaṇḍanam in a text parallel to idam agraṃ pāruṣyāṇāṃ yad utāryāṇāṃ avasphaṇḍanam, see; Tib. gnod pa, injure.
, adj. (ppp. of Skt. skhal, not cpd. with ava in Skt.; cf. Pali avakkhalita, n., offense), guilty, at fault; having offended: (tvaṃ hi) bhagavaty asakṛd-asakṛd avaskhalito.
, ppp. (= Pali avaṭṭhaddha, also with dental ttha; Skt. avaṣṭabdha, ppp. to ava-stambh), founded (upon), supported (by), in comp.: tīrthikāvastabdhaṃ tan nagaraṃ.
(to next but one with -aka), one who addresses contemptuously: bhikṣor gṛhapater ˚kasya, of a monk who speaks contemptuously to a householder.
, in ˚spa˚, nt. (n. act. to next, q.v.), ridicule or contemptuous treatment: (kṣamaś) ca bhavati parato 'vamānānām avahasanāvaspaṇḍana-durukta-durāgatādīnām … vacanapathānāṃ;, see avaskandanā.

, in ˚spa˚ (cf. Skt. sphaṇḍ, parihāse; see prec. two) ridicules or treats with contempt: (na ca bodhisattvo) yācanakam avahasati nāvaspaṇḍ˚; (na ca … bodhisattvaḥ param avahasati) nāvaspaṇḍ˚; avahasati avaspaṇḍ˚; mayā … gṛhapatir ˚ḍitaḥ; Tib. brñas thabs gyiso (gyis so ?), acted contemptuously (towards).
, nt. (Skt. id., snapping of the fingers,; possibly the same word, applied to ‘casual rejection’ of an argument?), reading of in and of s.v. Tib. sphrugs bsigs instead of apasphoṭana, q.v.
(? the same word recorded in ʼs gaṇa gahādi? cf. Skt. avasyandita), changing the meaning of oneʼs own words: nāvasyandanavacanaḥ.

, adj. (= Pali avassuta), wet, dripping, and so foul, rotten, orig. of a tree the inside of which is rotten, Pali (rukkhāni) antopūtīni avassutāni kasambujātāni; fig., usually in Pali, and in BHS, of evil monks: antarpūty (read as separate word, see antaḥpūti) avasrutaḥ; foll. by kaṣambaka-jātaḥ (see kaśambaka); antaḥpūtir ˚taḥ kaṣambaka-jātaḥ.

,) ppp. avasvāpita, osvā˚ (caus. to ava-svap-, in Skt. recorded only in ppp. avasupta, asleep,; but see osopati; note also Jain Skt. () avasvāpanikā and ˚panī,), put to sleep, asleep: (vs) te cāpy avasvāpitāḥ (so em., confirmed by Tib. ñal; mss. avasthāpitāḥ, avasaṃsthitāḥ); śayavatī (q.v., read prob. yaśavatī) osvāpitā devataiḥ, and 10 puravaraṃ osvāpitaṃ devataiḥ, … put to sleep by the gods. Cf. also apasvāpana, osvāpana.
, m., a high number: = Tib. bsam yas, or bsal yas (cf. avada).

, adj. (or subst.?), (1) (an ascetic practice) that consists of not going abroad in the rainy season: avārṣikair (sc. ātāpanaparitāpanaiḥ, l. 15); Tib. dbyar mi byuṅ ba; (2) (a monk) who does not observe the (rule for not wandering during the) rains:; read so with v.l. and in (Tib. dbyar gnas su ma zhugs pa).

, adj. n. sg. m. (or could be adv., acc. sg. nt.; = Pali avaṃsira(s), avasira(s), Skt. avākśiras), head downwards, headlong: = atha ( mā; so; mss. apparently lack any such word, except that one reads nā in) ghorarūpaṃ narakaṃ prapatiṣye avāśiro (so clearly the mss. read or intend; vv.ll. avāraśiro, avaśiro, unmetr.; em. avākśiro).
, ppp. (to Skt. ava-ā-sru-, not recorded; cf. Pali avassuta, taken by as from ava plus Skt. sru-), descending in floods: (vs, printed as prose) payomucaḥ … avāśrutāmbhaso.
(cf. vika˚; = Pali avikampana, [Page077-b] nt.), the not-wavering (from …, in comp.): samyakprayogāvikampanatā.

, adj. (= Pali avikiṇṇa-vāca), not loose, not uncontrolled, in speech: = (in both read: amukharā (ca?) abhū avikīrṇavācā; in prec. line acapalā, anuddhatā; these four adj. associated formulaically in Pali).

(nt.; = Pali id.), the not disturbing, non-confusion: bhūtakoṭy-avikopana-cakraṃ; dharmadhātv-avikopana-cakraṃ; parāvikopana-tvāt, because of the fact that it is not subject to disturbance by others (or, by foes).

(neg. ppp. of vikopayati, q.v.), unperturbed, undisturbed, unmoved: avikopitayā caryā (instr.); -avikopitajñāna-; avikopita (asthisaṃghāta, q.v.);;; replaced by avigopita, Bhagavataḥ śarīram ˚taṃ; (Tib. ma ñams pa, undisturbed; but in occurs vigopayati, opens, Tib. kha phye, see vigopita).

, (= Pali avitakka-jhāyī,), (devoted to the [2d] stage of dhyāna) in which there is no ratiocination:, avitarka- (mss. avitakāyaṃ, avitarkaṃ kāyaṃ)-dhyāyī (mss. -dhyāyino, which is possible in sense and meter and should perhaps be kept, despite the Pali parallel -jhāyī).
, f. (neg. to *vitṛpti, nowhere recorded; to vi-tṛp-), insatiableness: vedayato 'vitṛptis tṛṣṇā.
, adj. (= Pali id.; see avidvasu), ignorant: ˚su, n. sg. (or perhaps ˚sū, cf. ms. B in l. 16 abhiddaśū) is plausibly conjectured by for corrupt readings of mss. and 16.
, ignorance, occurs in (text without v.l.) in the place of abhidhyā in a list of the 10 karmapatha; certainly in some sense secondary and perhaps a mere textual corruption for abhidhyā, covetousness.

, adj. (Sktized form of aviddasu, q.v.; records but does not explain the Pali form, which seems to be a curious blend of Pali avidvā = Skt. a-vidvān with a-vidu, the s due to Skt. viduṣ-, cf. viduṣaka), ignorant: ˚sū, nom. pl.,; (avidvalāś);;; ˚sūnāṃ, gen. pl., (all vss).

, interj. (always repeated; most often followed by (i)ti; = Pkt. avihā, cf. avidā, avida, exclamation of sorrow,), exclamation of disapproval or dismay; only noted in; mss. sometimes abhi-for avi-, occasionally -dhāṃ for -dhaṃ or -dhā: avidhā avidhā; avidhāvidhaṃ (ti; so mss.); avidhāvidhā (usually followed by ti);;; ˚dhāṃ (mss.); ˚dheti (mss.); ˚dhaṃ or ˚dhan (ti);;; (mss.);;;. Rarely ā-is written in mss. for initial a-.
, adj. (= Pali ˚dhamma), not liable to fall (to evil existences): ˚dharmāṇaḥ, n. pl. m.

(m.; corresponds to Pali avinibbhoga; see also vinirbhāga; note avinirbhūta = avinirbhāgena avasthita; acc. to s.v. avinibbhutta, avinirbhūta = this Pali form ‘through confusion with a-vinā-bhūta’), non-differentiation, non-distinction, confusion:; (kleśānāṃ …) sahajāvinirbhāga-tāṃ, innate (natural) confusion;, see vinirbhāga;;, text avinirbhāva, v.l. ˚bhāga, which read with without v.l. (-varti, abiding in non-discrimination) = Tib. tha (so Tib. Index, misprinted thad in text) dad du mi ḥjug pa (or, gnas pa), not differing, not admitting of differentiation,.
, read avinirbhāga, q.v.; but cf. avinirbhūta, cited there.)
(see s.v. ˚tya), not liable to turning back: ˚ta-cittāśayamanaskārair, of Bodhisattvas in 3d bhūmi; in vs replaced by anivartiya, q.v.

, incapable of turning back (= avinivartya, q.v., etc.), of persons destined for enlightenment, commonly with the word Bodhisattva, often (e.g.;;) with dependent phrase anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau:;;;;;; as subst. m., n. of a Bodhisattva-samādhi:.
(Skt. not fleeing in battle,, see s.v.; here = avinivartya, anivarti(i)ya, avivart(i)ya, qq.v., etc.), not liable to turning back (religiously): bodhicittāvinivartinī (of a woman).
(= ˚ta, ˚tin, ˚tanīya; also avivart(i)ya, anivart(i)ya, avaivartika, qq.v.; in Pali only forms of anivatt-seem to be recorded), not liable to turning back: (prose).
, m. (neg. of vi˚, q.v.; = Pali avippaṭi sāra), absence of regret or remorse; contentment: ˚raḥ prāmodyaṃ; and ˚ra-saṃjananārthaṃ (in text ˚saṃjanārthaṃ). See the next entries.
, abstr. to next, state of non-discontent, absence of regrets: prītiṃ prāmodyam avipratisāritāṃ ca janayiṣyati (said of an act of giving).

, also ājaniya, ājānya, ājāniya, ājāneya, adj. (= Pali ājañña, ājāniya, ājānīya, ājāneyya), of noble race, blooded, primarily of animals, esp. horses; by extension used of men, esp. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and very rarely (meaning noble) of other, inanimate entities. Tib. (e.g., etc.) regularly renders caṅ śes (pa), omniscient, falsely interpreting the word as derived from jñā know. In composition, the word in all its forms regularly (not always) follows the noun, e.g. aśvājāneya, a blooded horse (orig. perhaps a thoroughbred of a horse?), below. As separate word: of animals, yo aśvavaraṃ damayed ājāneyan (= ˚yaṃ) va saindhavaṃ; ājāneyā hayottamāḥ;; cf. yuktāni ājānyarathāni chariots of (drawn by) blooded (horses), all hitched up; ājāneyau dvau balīvardhāv; ājăniyo hastipoto (prose, no v.l.); of men, ājāneyānāṃ sattvānāṃ; ˚neyaḥ, of śrāvakas; ˚neya ity ucyate, of the Tathāgata; ājāneyo kahin ti nāma (so em., mss. kāma) bhoti, answered by … ājāneyo (v.l. ˚ya) tam (em. ti tam) āhu bhūriprajñā (mss. ˚jño); voc. ājanya, addressed to Buddha, namas te muktāyājanya; cf. ājāneya-mānā, paying reverence to the Noble One (the Buddha); in and dāntājāneya-prāpta;; and 20 ājanyaprāpta, all of Bodhisattvas (cf. ājāneyā bodhisattvāḥ), become noble (steeds), see s.v. prāpta; the figure of a horse is surely intended here, since there is contrast with bodhisattva-khaḍuṅkāḥ, the latter (q.v.) being a term pertaining in its literal sense to horses; here may also belong ājāneya-vikrāntaṃ vikramantam, said of the Bodhisattva, striding with the stride of a blooded horse, or of a noble person (cf. the next following mahāpuruṣavikrāntaṃ vikr˚), but possibly striding with a noble stride (cf. the preceding aparājitavikrāntaṃ vikr˚), as in the next example; as prior member of karmadhāraya cpds. or bahuvrīhis based on them, occasionally noble, distinguished, in application to other than animate beings: catasra imā … ājāneya-gatayo bodhisattvenānugantavyāḥ, noble procedures (listed as sugatipratilābha, guruśuśrūṣaṇā, prāntaśayyāsanābhirati, pratibhānapratilābha; is the literal meaning gaits of a blooded horse?); ājāneya-svaraḥ could, then, also be taken as having a noble sound (ep. of the Buddhaʼs voice), but in view of the preceding vṛṣabhasvaraḥ and the following krauñcasvaraḥ it probably means having the sound of a blooded (horse) and belongs above; once, at least, this adj. precedes in composition the name of the animal to which it is applied, ājāneya-hasty-upetān; but regularly this order is reversed (as in such cpds. as nara-śārdūla) and we find aśvājāneya, m. (lit. thoroughbred of a horse) (misunderstood s.v. ājāneya);;; (mss.);; (ms. aśvāyāneyān); bhadrāśvājāneya-; hastyājāneya;;; siṃhājāneya; and (cf. above, and Pali purisājāneyya) by extension puruṣājāneya (the corruptions puruṣăjāneya and ˚ṣajāna occur in mss. and sometimes in edd.), corresponds to;;; in ed. em. puruṣājāniyam, mss. corrupt, [Page090-b] reading doubtful; puruṣājanya (vs); (voc., to the Buddha).

, adj. (= Pali attamana(s), which is also, but less often, represented by āptamana(s), q.v., on which cf. s.v. attamanas, which fails to note occurrence of āpta˚ in BHS), glad at heart, delighted; esp. in certain formulas; applied to the audience at the end of a discourse by Buddha, e.g. idam avocad bhagavān, āttamano (n. sg. m.) āyuṣmān Mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandat; idam avocad bhagavān, āttamanasas te bhikṣavo 'bhyanandan; often in a series of synonyms, as tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ;; plurals of the same words; and variations, as hṛṣṭā tuṣṭā āttamanā (n. pl. m.) pramudita-prītisaumanasyajātā; more briefly, tuṣṭo āttamano abhūt; tuṣṭo āttamanā (n. sg. m.) imaṃ udānam udānaye (aor.); dātāraṃ ca dṛṣṭvā āttamanā bhavati sumanaskaḥ; sattvā āttamanaso 'bhūvan; Indra āttamanā (n. sg. m.) tasyāṃ velāyāṃ …; dṛṣṭvā ca bhavati (bhoti) āttamanā (n. sg. f.) =; doubled (intensive āmreḍita), sā 'ttamanāttamanā(ḥ) she, greatly delighted,;; so 'py āttamanāttamanā(ḥ);; similarly; neg. anāttamanā(ḥ) (follows atiśayitaroṣaś caṇḍībhūto). Once printed attamanas, q.v. This word is to be analyzed as a cpd. of Skt. ātta, ppp. of ā-dā, with manas. The alternant āptamanas is analyzable as āpta, ppp. of āp (cf. manaāpa, manāpa) plus manas. Pali attamana(s) could represent both; both may be Sktizations of that MIndic form.
, adj. = āttamanas: ˚kaḥ; fem., (pramodāmi) ˚kā bhavāmi; comp. ˚kataro 'bhūn; abstr. n. ˚ka-tā state of being delighted.
(or -attamīya), semi-MIndic for -ātmīya, in attāttamīya, q.v.

(m.: = Pali atta-gāha), belief in the (existence of a) self; see -grāha.

, adj., also subst. nt. (= Pali attaniya), own, oneʼs own (= sva, adj., or ātmanaḥ, gen.): (prose) ˚yāś ca duhitrīr (acc. pl.;), his own daughters; usually quasi-subst., what pertains to the self, what is of the nature of the self (the existence of which is denied): [Page092-b] (see under -grāha); (vs) cakṣur na istri puruṣo na pi cātmanīyaṃ; (vs) strī neha nāsti ca pumān na ca ātmanīyaṃ; (vs) yasyeha ātmā (read nātmā? Tib. and Chin. render the neg. twice) na ca ātmanīyam (so read, text ˚yām); and 14—15 naivātmā naivātmanīyā śūnyā ātmena vā ātmanīyena vā (so, prob. rightly; mss. corrupt, esp. in 8); śūnyā an-ātmanīyā (Bhvr., having nothing that pertains to the self) ātmena vā ātmanīyena vā.

, m. (rarely nt.), (= Pali attabhāva, listed by Pali Lex. among words denoting body,), body, synonym of śarīra: śirāṃsi kecin nayanāni kecid dadanti kecit pravarātmabhāvān; darśinsu te mahya tadātmabhāvaṃ; ātmabhāvapratilambhenaiva bhagavan sarvakrīḍanakāni labdhāni bhavanti, only by rescuing their own bodies …; dīrghātmabhāvā hi bhavanti, of long bodies; puruṣātmabhāvaṃ ca yadā labhante, and when they get a human body;;; -stūpe tathāgatasyātmabhāvas tiṣṭhaty ekaghanas …; mahātmabhāvā rūpeṇa, great-bodied in form;; ātmabhāvaparityāgena, by sacrifice of oneʼs body; divyamanomayātmabhāvapratilabdhāḥ; mātuḥ-kukṣigatasyātmabhāvo 'bhinirvṛtto 'bhūt;; -kākagṛdhro-(mss. gṛddho-; gṛdho-, misprint?) -lūkagaruḍādisadṛśātmabhāvāḥ, having bodies like …; āyāmato bahuyojanaśatikena ātmabhāvena; abhedyo siṃhārdhapūrvo bhagavato ātmabhāvo; (pūyaṃ yakṛdvṛkkaphuṣphasehi) gūthaṃ ca anyaṃ anugatam ātmabhāve; asīhi chinnā bahuvidham ātmabhāvā; te nirmiṇitvā vikṛtātmabhāvāṃ, distorted bodies;;; ˚va-pratilambhe, attainment of a body, reincarnation; same; yojanaśatikā ātmabhāvā, and the like; ˚va-pratilambhe (as above); same cpd.; as nt., perhaps by attraction to associated form of śarīra, yuṣmākam etāny ātmabhāvāni saṃtarpayed mahataujasā yuṣmākam etāni divyāni śarīrāṇi vivardhayet; (vs) tyaktā maya ātmabhāvāḥ; (cpd. with list of bodily members, ending) -hṛdaya-sarvātmabhāva-parityāgo; others,;;;;;;;;;;;;;;; could be indefinitely extended (very common in most texts). The fact has not been recognized sufficiently clearly that this is a quite plain and simple synonym of śarīra, body. The same is in general true of Pali, tho I am not prepared to say that it always has that mg. there. The Pali dictionaries (even) do not bring this out clearly.

, ʼs em. (prose) sarvatra bodhisattvasya ˚tām anuprāptāṃ saṃjānanti; should mean embodiment, from ātmabhāva plus -tā. But the occasion is the approach to his enlightenment (not his conception or birth), which is signalized by miracles and cosmic portents. The mss. read ˚bhāvanām, which is doubtless right: they recognize on all sides that the Bodhisattvaʼs self-realization (ātma-bhāvanā) is at hand.]

(ppp.) perh. to be read in (vs) where all mss. mūrdhnā (one ms. adds ca) dārito bhūmau (one syllable short, without ca); if we read ādārito (or ādarito; ppp. denom. from ādara?) meter would be correct; it should mean prostrated in respectful salutation with the head on the ground. , beginning (= Skt.): ādiṃ, acc. (= Pali ādiṃ katvā, with acc. object) and ādau, loc., with following kṛtvā, and preceding acc. (once gen.), lit. putting … first; so beginning with, starting with, from … on (the loc. ādau used precisely like the acc. ādiṃ; putting at the beginning = making the beginning; loc. only in): tuṣitabhavanavāsam ādiṃ kṛtvā, beginning with (the Bodhisattvaʼs) dwelling in the Tuṣita-heaven (= from then on) =, cf. tuṣitabhavanam ādau kṛtvā sarveṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ …; āvīcim ādiṃ kṛtvā sarvanairayikāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ …, of all hell-inhabitants [Page093-b] from Āvīci on; mātuḥ kukṣim ādau kṛtvā bodhisattvānāṃ yāvat parinirvṛtā, beginning with the motherʼs womb, of Bodhisattvas, until they have entered complete nirvāṇa; bhartāraṃ ādau kṛtvā (no man has any carnal desire for the destined mothers of Buddhas) from their husbands on; bodhisattvasya garbhāvakrāntim ādau kṛtvā; śākyamuniṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ ādau kṛtvā ḍaśa bhūmayo deśitā, beginning from (the time of) Śākyamuni the Buddha, the Ten Stages have been taught (not before! so, I think, the parallels require us to interpret, contrary to); with gen. of the dependent noun (rather than acc.), evidently construed as modifier of ādiṃ: tṛṣṇāyāḥ paunarbhavikyā ādiṃ kṛtvā, beginning with (starting from; lit. making a beginning of) desire for rebirth. Cf. Crit. ed. saha strībhir draupadīm ādi-kṛtvā, along with the women, beginning with Draupadī (i.e. Draupadī and the others). This seems to be unparalleled in Skt. See also s.v. ādīkaroti.
, adj. (= Pali id., see; Mahāvaṃsa phalaṃ … ādikaṃ), first, initial:.

, adj. and subst., = prec. (which replaces this two lines below): ˚miṇāṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ …

(formally looks like passive to ā-dā; = Pali ādiyati, only with short i; cf. upād˚, paryād˚, samād˚; all these regularly used with active mg., except paryādīyante [and this is uncertain; cites it as parihīyante]; in Pali also active mg., except sometimes pariyādiyati, pass.,; calls these forms ‘passive with middle meaning’; I prefer the term ‘active’), takes; takes on, assumes: (yaṃ nūnāhaṃ) adinnaṃ anyātakaṃ (q.v.) śālim ādiyeyaṃ (v.l. ādī˚), opt., and (11) ādiyeya (v.l. ˚yaṃ, ādī˚) 3 sg. pret., also (12) ādiyantaṃ (v.l. ādī˚), acc. sg. pres. pple.; (vs) puṣpaṃ tyajitvā phalam ādiyante (mss. ˚nta, to be kept as imperf.?); (bhavān …) dhanam ādiyatu (v.l. ādī˚); (bhavān …) striyaḥ ādiyatu; (yo imāṃ saṃskārāṃ) ādīyati (no v.l.) vā nikṣipati vā.

, (1) (cf. Hindi ādes salutation, late Skt. ādeśa id.,), salutes, greets: ˚śitavya, gdve., (na bhikṣavo) yuṣmābhir ādiśitavyaṃ bhikṣāyāṃ labdhāyāṃ, monks, you must not salute (the [Page094-a] donor) when you have received alms; (2) (= Pali ādisati, obj. dakkhinaṃ, dānaṃ), assigns (the profit from a meritorious act, ordinarily a gift of alms to the Buddha and his monks; object dakṣiṇām, once dakṣiṇādeśanām; this profit is, at the desire of the donor, often assigned by the recipient, ordinarily the Buddha, to the credit of someone else, e.g. a tormented preta, or the deceased father of the donor): bhagavatābhihitaḥ: mahārāja, kasya nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādiśāmi, kiṃ tavāho svid yena tavāntikāt prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasūtam iti (similarly, etc.), the Lord said: O King, in whose name shall I assign the profit of your gift? yours, or that of one who has produced more merit than you?; tato bhagavān … dakṣiṇām ādiśati (in a verse,, assigning it to the benefit of pretas); bhagavāṃś ca … dakṣiṇādeśanām ādiśati (as prec.); tato bhagavatā pretasya nāmnā dakṣiṇā ādiṣṭā; but the same ādiśati may be used when the subject is the donor, as in a frequent cliché in which a man hopes to have a son who will assign to him after death the profit of gifts and works of merit: asmākaṃ ca (see atyatīta) … dānāni dattvā puṇyāni kṛtvā nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādiśed, … he would assign the profit (of the gifts and virtuous acts) in my name; virtually the same ādekṣyati; and etc. ādekṣyate; but elsewhere, (3) when the donor (not the Buddha) is the subject, the caus. ādeśayati is used; so in the same cliché just mentioned, … dakṣiṇām ādeśayiṣyati, (my son …) will cause the profit to be assigned (to me); putraka … mama nāmnā buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojaya dakṣiṇām ādeśaya …; (asmākaṃ) ca nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādeśaya (also addressed by a father to his son). See s.v. dakṣiṇādeśanā.

(see s.v. ādi), starts from (acc.), makes the starting point: ger. ˚kariyāṇa, (vs) avidya (acc.) ādīkariyāṇa cakṣumān, prabhāṣate maraṇam anantaduḥkham (so apparently mss., combining the note to ed. with that to), starting with ignorance, the Enlightened One expounded death and {{infinit->infinite||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} misery. This reading is perfect in meter and sense. Possibly ādī is to be taken as a separate word, = ādiṃ; certainly it means the same as ādiṃ kṛ-.

, m. or (rarely) nt., once perh. adj., (= Pali id.; clearly Buddhist word, despite rare occurrences in late Skt., and despite ādĭnava-darśa in Vedic, see, s.v. ādīnava, and), misery, evil, danger, mishap, wretchedness: nt. noted only tāye atra mahādīnavaṃ utpāditaṃ; m. (unambiguously) ˚vaḥ; and ˚vo (mishap) 'tra bhaviṣyati; ime cānye ādīnavā madyapāne; kṛtā kāmeṣv ādīnavakathā, gṛhāśramapadasyādīnavo bhāṣitas; yaḥ kaścid ādīnavo, any disaster whatever (may occur); same,; tathā daśādīnavā Nandikasūtra uktāḥ prāṇātipātasya; pañcatriṃśad ādīnavāḥ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthāne; often with loc. of that in, or in connection with, which the evil is manifested, as, kāmeṣu ādīnavaṃ dṛṣṭvā;;;; mitreṣu ādīnavaṃ (read ˚va, m.c.) saṃmṛśanto (vs); taṃ tiryagyoniṣu mahantaṃ ādīnavaṃ dṛṣṭvā, similarly;; dṛṣṭvā ādīnavaṃ loke; other locs. above and below; but occasionally gen. instead, kāyasyādīnavaṃ saṃpaśyan; prāṇātipātasya (above); or prior member in comp., saṃsāra-doṣādīnava-niḥśaraṇa-(= niḥsa˚)-kuśalaḥ; lokādīnavaṃ lokaniḥsaraṇam api deśayāmi; in contrast with āsvāda, āsvādādīnaveṣu in enjoyments and miseries; kāmāna āsvādaṃ … ādīnavaṃ ca kāmānāṃ bhāṣate puruṣottamaḥ (vs); others, miscellaneous, ahaṃ ca ādīnava (acc.) tatra darsayīṃ (˚yī) (vs); taṃ kampille [Page094-b] mahāntam ādīnavaṃ dṛṣṭvā; etam ādīnavaṃ ācikṣiṣyāmi; ādīnavadarśāvī (= Pali ˚dassāvi-n) perceiving the misery or danger, n. sg. of ˚vin, kāmeṣu; (here text ˚darśī, v.l. ˚darśāvī); without dependent noun, ˚śāvī, followed by niḥsaraṇa- (or niḥśa˚; delete final -ḥ in the first passage) -prajñaḥ (or -prājño);; ˚va-darśin = ˚va-darśāvin, tatrādīnavadarśinaḥ (tatra = strīṣu); in Bhvr. cpds., (kāmāḥ) sabhayāḥ saraṇāḥ sādīnavāḥ sadoṣā iti; anantādīnavā mārṣa kāmāḥ; bahvādīnavaś ca gṛhāvāso; once apparently ādīnava alone, uncompounded, used as adj., wretched, evil, miserable, (vs) sarvaṃ ādīnavaṃ lokaṃ (parallel with ādīpitaṃ, prajvalitaṃ, prakampitaṃ, in same vs applied to lokaṃ).
, adj. (= Skt. ādīpta plus -ka), ablaze, on fire: (vs) ˚ke jvālasahasrapūrṇe (sc. gṛhe); perhaps ka m.c.

, nt. (anomalously m. ˚yaḥ = Tib. bdaṅ du ḥgyur ba (or bya ba), so also; = Pali ādhipateyya, see below; from adhipati, roughly = Skt. ādhipatya, which is used in, see Index, in ways not closely parallel to the Pali usage), control, influence, mastery, prime motivation (lit. overlordship). In Pali esp. used of one of three influences leading to virtue, attādhi˚ (q.v.), lokādhi˚, dhammādhi˚, see s.v. ādhipateyya and (the influence of oneself, i.e. conscience or self-respect; the influence of the world or public opinion; the influence of dhamma or regard for moral principles as authoritatively laid down). In BHS little evidence is found for the existence of these, tho () renders (hrīvarṇapratisaṃyukteṣu) lokādhipateyeṣu ca (sc. upaneyam) by … the regard of public opinion, perhaps rightly. On the other hand, lokādhipateya-prāpta can only mean arrived at the overlordship of the world; it is one of a long list of epithets of the Buddha as the one that has ‘turned the wheel of the Law’; it is preceded by lokagurur … lokārthakara … lokānuvartaka … lokavid ity ucyate, and it would be absurd to interpret it as under the control of public opinion. (See also s.v. ādhipateyatā.) = = = (evaṃ khalu) punaḥ ādhipateya-mātram etaṃ tatropatteḥ, but this, of course, is only the principal cause (controlling influence) of rebirth there (viz. in one of various hells); na tad balaṃ na tad ādhipateyaṃ … (saṃvidyate), that (sort of) power or controlling influence (is not found); oftener at the end of Bhvr. cpds., mahākaruṇādhipateyaṃ, (any action of Bodhisattvas is …) controlled (influenced) by supreme compassion; cakṣurindriyādhipateyā rūpārambaṇaprativijñaptiḥ, recognition of the sense-object form, which (recognition) is controlled by (= dependent on) the sense of sight; (tac cittam utpadyate bodhisattvānāṃ) mahākaruṇāpūrvamgamaṃ prajñājñānādhipateyaṃ …; dharmādhipateya, of Buddhas. See next.

(from prec.), (1) state of overlordship or control; (2) at the end of Bhvr. cpds. ending in ˚teya-, state of being under the control of … (lit. state of having … as controlling influence); (1) (pūrvaṃ mayā svayaṃbhuvām) ādhipateyatām abhilaṣatā, of old by me (Buddha) desiring supremacy over (first place among) Self-existent Ones; -puṇyasaṃbhārabalaviśeṣaṇāsadṛśī- (better would seem to be ˚sadṛśīṃ, which [Page095-b] is read by Calc. but none of ʼs mss.) -lokādhipateyatāṃ saṃdarśya, (said of the Bodhisattva) manifesting an unexampled state of mastery over the world thru …; (2) buddhādhipateyatāṃ, state of being under the control of the Buddhas; supratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣor maitryādhipateyatayā, … because he is under the influence of love; cittam … rājasadṛśaṃ sarvadharmādhipateyatayā (so read for text ˚pateyā, uninterpretable), (in a passage decrying the vanity of cittam,) citta is like a king, because it is controlled by all the states of (conditioned, transitory) existence; at least, this mg. seems more consistent with the context than because it is the ruler of all states …, but this latter is what Tib. means (chos thams cad la dbaṅ byed paḥi phyir); in that case to 1.

(in Skt. as subst. nt., unmittelbare Folge,, or unmittelbares Darauf, … Nachher,; cf. ˚rīya, anantariya, and next, also upānantarīya); as subst. nt., not limited to evil connotation and much as in Skt., bodhicitto- (1st ed. ˚catto-; corr. 2d ed.)-tpādapraśaṃsāparaṃparānantaryāṇi, enlightenment-thought-production-laudation-series-immediacies, and a long series of terms ending likewise in ˚paraṃparānantaryāṇi, actions or events succeeding one another immediately, ending in bodhisattvasusūkṣmajñānapraveśaparaṃparānantaryāṇi, tāny asyāḥ sarvaromavivarebhyo nirmāṇakāyameghān niścaritvā sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayamānān (read ˚mānāny?) apaśyat; upapatty-ānantarya-citte (but here perhaps as adj.) the mental state which immediately precedes rebirth (see upapatti); perhaps in same sense ānantarya-mārgaḥ, of the 8-fold noble path as characterized by immediate succession (of its stages, one after another) or causing immediate results, as below; the latter surely in pañcemāni … ānantaryāṇi yair ānantaryaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvāḥ kṣipram anuttarā (read ˚rāṃ) samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyate (read ˚yante?); here translate continuities, but better procedures bringing immediate, speedy (desirable) results (note kṣipram; the five are listed in what follows); see also ānantaryasamādhi; otherwise the word has been noted only as adj. with karman, or subst. nt. without karman; (evil) action bringing immediate retribution, deadly sin (= Pali ānatariya or ˚rika, with or sc. kamma, see s.v. pañcānantariyakammaṃ); there are five [Page096-a] such, viz. killing of mother, father, or an arhant, causing dissension in the order of monks, and deliberately causing a Tathāgataʼs blood to flow (same list in Pali): pañcānantaryāṇi (Kyoto ed. ˚tarīyāṇi but ˚taryāṇi; list of 5 given); (with list); ˚ryāṇi kṛtāni (listed and described in the following, down to) etāni pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṛtvā mahānarakeṣūpapanno; and (without karmāṇi); pañcānantaryakariṇasyāpi, even of a doer of …; (after a list of the five crimes) ebhiḥ pañcabhir ānantaryaiḥ karmabhir …; two or three of the list mentioned, yadā tasya trīṇy ānantaryāṇi paripūrṇāni … pāpa eṣa pitṛghātako 'rhadghātako mātṛghātakaś ca, trīṇy anenānantaryāṇi narakakarmasaṃvartanīyāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni; dve tvayā ānantarye karmaṇī kṛte (killing of father and of an arhant bhikṣu); others, ˚rya-karma-kāriṇāṃ … sattvānāṃ; ˚ryam karma kṛtvā; ˚rya-kāriṇaḥ … sattvān.

(= Pali id.), breath (see below): ˚na-bhāvanā-vidhiḥ; ˚na-smṛti (= Pali ˚na-sati), mindfulness [Page096-b] of breathing,;;;;; ˚nānusmṛti, id.,; on this and (where text ānāpā-nusmṛtir) see s.v. anusmṛti. The word is an old dvandva; āna (= prāṇa) plus apāna (cf. Skt. prāṇāpāna, on which see). In Pali commentarial diction replaced by assāsa-passāsa (= āśvāsa-praśvāsa, q.v.). It is clear that Tib. understands āna = āśvāsa as inbreathing, apāna = praśvāsa as outbreathing. There is BHS evidence supporting this interpretation of āśvāsa-praśvāsa, q.v.

(= ant˚, q.v.; some cases there cited may belong here), space between, interval, interstice: gopānasy-āntarikāś (n. pl.), interstices of the roof-frame; ekaikasyāṃ ca nady-āntarikāyāṃ, and in each interval between the rivers.
(so; Kyoto ed. indicates both this and āntarī˚ as var. readings), m. pl. ˚naḥ, dwelling in the atmosphere, n. of a class of gods:; = antarikṣa, ˚rīkṣa, ˚rīkṣecara, qq.v.; see also deva.
, m. (pl.), = antra-guṇa, q.v.:;; read in both (āntram) āntraguṇā(ḥ). (In could be intended as well as antra˚.)

(= Pali id., thematization of Skt. āp, ap), water; clear cases noted only in cpd. āpa-skandha mass of water, (vs) sa caiva sama muñceta āpaskandham analpakam; with adhaḥ or heṣṭā, heṣṭi, of subterranean mass of water, adha-āpaskandham; (vs) [Page097-b] heṣṭāpaskandha (acc. sg.; so divide) caraṇaiḥ pratigrāhyamāṇāḥ, being caused to receive with their feet the mass of water underneath (the earth); (vs) heṣṭi śatasahasraṃ yāvataś cāpaskandho (contrasted with dharaṇitalu, next line). In (vs) āpaṃ, acc. sg., could be referred to this stem, or regarded as belonging to the Skt. stem āp, ap, transferred to the sing. (cf.).
, n. of a grove at Sāṃkāśya:.
, in comp. (= Pali id.; rare in Skt., see), dealer, shopkeeper: pitā te gāndhikāpaṇika āsīd, perfume-shopkeeper.

, f. (= Pali and Skt. Lex. id.), sin (see also anāpatti, mūlāpatti): ˚tiḥ; naiḥsargikāpattiḥ (so correctly Index and; see naiḥsargika); ˚tyā codayati, see this; duṣṭhulām (q.v.) āpattim; abhīkṣṇāpatti-āpadyana-tā state of constantly committing sins (cf. abhīkṣṇāpattika); (bodhisattvasy)āpattir api veditavyā; ˚ty-anadhyācāra-vyutthāne; (see s.v. anadhyāpatti); five groups of sins to which monks may be subject, comm., see.
= āpatti in Bhvr. cpd.; see an-ā˚, abhīkṣṇāpattika, sāpattika.
(Pali and Skt. Lex. id., Skt. āpad; cf.), disaster: āpadāsu;.

, also ˚na-tā (from āpadyate, ˚ti, with suffix ana, n. act.), the getting into, or commission (of a sin): (prose) abhīkṣṇāpatti-āpadyana-tā, see s.v. āpatti; (vs) na te bheje devamukhyānāṃ (bad meter!) tarjanyāpadyanālaye (? obscure; app. tarjanī, or a case-form of it, compounded with or followed by cpd. of āpadyana and ālaya).
, ppp.-adj. (to āpatti), guilty of a sin (is Pali āpanna so used without complement?): yad uta, āpanna iti vā anāpanna iti vā.
, f. ˚kī, adj. (from aparānta, q.v., plus ika), future, of the future: (prose) āparāntikāvīcikaduḥkhena (2d ed. ˚khe); (cited) eṣāparāntiky apekṣā.
(recorded once in), beholds: (prose) sattvān āpaśyati sma (so with best mss.); doubtful; in parallel all mss. and both edd. paśyati, with v.l. here.

, m., action of water: (na tasya caurā rājāno dhanaskandha [so one ms., with v.l. ˚dhaṃ] parāmṛṣe) agnir vā āpaskaro (read ˚kāro?) vā (one ms. om. vā; em. apaskaroti, very implausibly) pūjāṃ kṛtvā tathāgate.

, adj. = āpāyika (apāya with suffix -a), in paścaināṃś codayiṣyāmo bhūtam āpāya-gocarān, and afterwards we will incite them who are veritably in a sphere-of-existence characterized by evil fate. So if text be kept; note states that Tib. (sdig med) points to apāpa-, and translate with this, so that they may … be beyond the sphere of sin.
(cf. āpāyita, āpyāyaka), giving to drink, nourishing: ˚kaṃ poṣakaṃ saṃvardhakaṃ.

, f. ˚kī, adj. and subst. (= Pali id.; from apāya with suffix ika), pertaining or leading to an evil fate (such as existence in hell); subst., one doomed to, or suffering, such an existence: ˚ke karmaṇi ca pravṛttā; tena dṛṣṭivyasanopanipātenāpāyikena lokānarthākarabhūtena; tīvrām āpāyikīṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanām; āyatyām āpāyikaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavati; ˚ka-kleśa-pakṣyasya; ˚kaṃ karma; subst., (vs) āpāyikā nirvṛtā brahmalokaṃ (cf. Pali); (vs) āpāyiko nairayiko.
, ppp. (cf. āpāyaka; to ā-pā-, caus.), given [Page098-a] to drink, nourished: ˚tā poṣitā saṃvardhitā. This and āpāyaka together forbid em. to āpyāy-. The same three ppp. stems;.

(= Skt. āpīḍa, chaplet, wreath), only in ˚ka-jāta hung with wreaths, noted only as ep. of trees: ˚ka-jātam (context suggests that it was prob. epithet of a tree, or at least referred to trees); ˚ka-jātān (vṛkṣān);; ˚ka-jātāḥ (phalavṛkṣāḥ) (so certainly read as suggested in note; text with mss. āpīnaka-).
, in (-hūṇ)āpīrā (sc. lipi), n. of some kind of writing: (v.l. ˚āpirā or ˚ro). would understand abhīrā (preferably the regular Skt. ābhīrā).

(also ˚nas-ka,) = āttamanas, q.v.:, Obv. 3 idam avocat bhagavān, āptamanas (read ˚manasas) te bhikṣavo …; Rev. 5, same phrase, reading ˚manasas; cf. (erroneously rendered with receptive mind);; āptamanā, n. sg. m.; neg. anāptamanā(ḥ), n. sg. m., abhiṣaktaḥ kupitaḥ caṇḍīkṛto 'nāpta˚; abhiṣakta-kupitaś caṇḍīkṛto 'nāpta˚.

, nt. (gdve. of āp-), what can be received (of food), oneʼs fill: (ghṛtasya madhunaś) cāpyaṃ pūrayitvā, having given (the infant) all he could eat of ghee and honey; so app. Tib. de ḥdraṇs par bsñod nas.
, adj. or subst. (m.), nourishing, nourisher: putrasya mātāpitarāv āpyāyakau poṣakau … Cf. āpāyaka (which perh. read?).

, adj. (possibly read apr˚? corresp. to Pali apaṇṇa-ka, q.v. in; cf. apaṇṇakaṅga, unique or universal factor; etymology unknown), perfect, in āprāṇyāṅga, of perfect qualities: (see,) (nihitaṃ tu tato kṛtvā dhūpayet karpūradhūpanaiḥ; read with) āprāṇyāṅga-samutthaṃ vā (, ou avec un produit sans parcelles vivantes, etymologizing as from a-prāṇa) kuṅkumacandanādibhiḥ. The evident correspondence between our word and Pali apaṇṇa(ka) makes ʼs interpretation hardly possible. Our word is a secondary hyper-Sktism, but the history of it remains quite unknown.

, adj. or subst. (Skt. ābaddha, with suffix ka, perhaps specifying,), (something that is) tied on (as an ornament): (prose) tasyāpi rājño śatasahasramūlyo hāro ābaddhako, tasya ca hārasya …; (prose) yo kumārasya hāro ābaddhako mahāraho śatasahasramūlyo, so hāro …; = (vs) ābaddhakā manuṣyāṇāṃ (apparently agreeing with words in prec. line which reads by em. hārā and niṣkāni [sic, ˚ni]; the mss. are very corrupt).

, adj., lit. having tied oneʼs girdle, i.e. girded oneʼs loins, or freely, vigorously setting out upon action: ˚raḥ; Tib. renders approximately going out without being touched at all; Chin. (walking) without leaning on others (or, without help of others).
, adj. (from Skt. ābandha with suffix ya), serving or intended for binding, capturing (animals): mamāmī kūṭāḥ pāśālepāś cābandhyāḥ (said by a hunter).

, adj. (= Pali id.; from Skt. ābādha with suffix ika), sick, ailing: tasya pratyekabuddhasya pittābādhikasya (v.l. ˚dhitasya); ābādhikānāṃ sattvānāṃ vyādhitānāṃ; bhikṣur ābādhiko duḥkhito;, read ābādhiko for text ābodhiko. See also vāyv-ābādhika.
(cf. Pali abbāhana, abbūhana, nom. act.), instrument for extraction (of thorns, splinters, etc.): (prose) ābṛṃhaṇabhūtaṃ satkāyaśalyasamābṛṃhaṇatayā. Said of bodhicitta.

, ppp. of ābṛhati, in ābṛḍha-śalya (= Pali abbūḷha-salla), having the sting (of craving) pulled out: (v.l. ābrīḍha˚, so, with v.l. āvṛṭa˚) = Tib. (zug-rṅu) byuṅ ba; cf. āvrīḍha, to āvarhati, This word, in some form, is certainly intended by the corrupt āpraṭṭa-śalya of; and by text (vicikitsā-kathaṃkathā-śalyaḥ samūla) ārūḍho, where presumably read ābūḍho, see Pali above; (same passage) āvṛḍho.

(and āvṛhati; see also āvṛṃhati) both occur in Skt. in mg. extracts, draws out, and in Pali as abbahati, abbuhati, abbū˚, abbāheti, id. (as, thorns); both are so used also in BHS; but in BHS they both (oftener, it seems, spelled with v) have also the meaning exclusively noted for āvarhati, restores (a monk to good standing), which in Pali is abbheti (noun, abbhāna), apparently from Skt. āhvayati. I shall record such mgs., even where texts read āb˚, under āvarhati; in BHS the two groups are not clearly distinguishable. They may even be identical in origin, as holds, (withdrawal of offences committed by the monk implies restoration to good standing); so also in essence, tho doubtfully,. But on this theory it is hard to explain Pali abbheti (abbhāna), and I incline to believe that BHS has a secondary and confused blend, in which a form close to the Pali, meaning recall, was adapted to the word meaning extract, remove.

, m. pl. (= Pali id., misprinted once Abha, see s.v. Abhā), n. of a class of rūpāvacara gods, of the 2d dhyāna-bhūmi, see deva (only in a few lists): ābhā devā(ḥ); ābhā (v.l. ābhāś) ca (sc. devāḥ); ābhāṃ (acc. pl.; v.l. ăbhā) paśyati devatāṃ (v.l. ˚tāḥ).

, only in comp. with saṃbhakṣaṇa, q.v., and associated with other social activities; perhaps feasting (in groups); distinction from saṃbhakṣaṇa is not clear: āvāha-vivāhābhakṣaṇa-saṃbhakṣaṇeṣv evaṃbhāgīyeṣu (sc. parakṛtyeṣu,) sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchati; (after āvāha-vivāhārthikānāṃ) ābhakṣaṇa-saṃbhakṣaṇārthikānāṃ kṛtyasahāyārthikānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ … Neither word is known in this use outside BHS.

, ornament, as m. (recorded only as nt. in Skt., Pali, and Pkt.): (vs) ye (so, or ye hy, all mss.; ed. em. yā) ābharaṇā bhavanti … vicitrarūpāḥ (so all Nep. mss.; ed. ˚pā); (vs) sarve ābharaṇā vikīrṇa patitā muhyanti te vāriṇā, and 18 (with mss.) bhartuś cābharaṇā (acc. pl.; with adṛśi 15) savastramukuṭāṃ śayyāgatāṃ vyākulāṃ (omits the three anusvāras).
, n. of the pool into which the Bodhisattvaʼs ornaments were cast:.
, addresses insultingly: (kulastrī …) ākruṣṭā bhavaty ābhāṣṭā(ḥ) parāmṛṣṭā vā; Tib. kha ṅan smras, bad-mouth-speak.

, m. (in Pali only in the Skt. meaning of light, radiance; so also in BHS, e.g.), appearance and hence range, scope, of sense organs:, where each of the external (bāhirāṇi) āyatanāni (i.e. the objects of sense) comes into the range of the corresponding internal (ādhyātmikāni) āyatanāni (i.e. the sense organs or powers), e.g. rūpo ca bāhiraṃ āyatanaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ ābhāsam āgataṃ bhavati. In a similar Pali passage,, āpātha takes the place of our ābhāsa. Similarly manuṣyāṇāṃ śrotābhāsam āgacchati, comes within the range of menʼs hearing; cakṣuṣa ābhāsam āgacchanti; [Page099-a] santy anābhāsagatāḥ (see anābhāsa) sattvā ye mama cakṣuṣa ābhāsaṃ nāgacchanti; śrotendriyasyābhāsam āgacchanti; cakṣuṣa ābhāsam āgacchati. In same mg. avabhāsa, q.v. 2.
(see ābhāsa), comes into range, into play; becomes perceptible: … nimitta-samudācāro vā nābhāsībhavati.

, m., generally pl. (= Pali ābhassara; cf. ābhasvara), one (usually the 3d) of the classes of rūpāvacara gods in the 2d dhyāna-bhūmi (see deva): sing. of one of the class, (see Prabhāvyūha); mahābrahmā ˚raḥ prabhāsvaraḥ śuddhābhaḥ etc.; in also sg. in a list of sg. deities; ābhāsvare devanikāye, as a place of happy rebirth, in this class of gods (or in their dwelling-place); several times in this place or state of existence is mentioned as the abode of creatures in general, or of a Buddha and his disciples, in interim periods between world aeons, after destruction and before re-creation of the world, so ābhāsvare devanikāye upapadyanti, and 6—7 ˚rād devanikāyato cyavitvā; similarly;; pl. of the class as a whole,;;;;;;;;;;;;;, etc.; in named as an example of creatures in the third sattvāvāsa (q.v.), characterized as ekatvakāyā nānātvasaṃjñinas.

, adj. and subst., repeatedly in = Skt. ābhicārika, pertaining to (hostile, black) magic or as subst. (perh. by ellipsis of karman) a performance or practice of (hostile, black) magic:; ˚keṣu sarveṣu (subst.); ˚ka-kāṣṭhāni; ardharātre sthite candre kuryāt karmābhicārukam;;; ˚ka-karmāṇi; (aśeṣaṃ karma) karoti, varjayitvā kāmopasaṃhitam, ābhicārukaṃ ca; in contrasted with śāntika, pacifying (performance), as antonym, ābhicāruke mahāmāṃsena, śāntike mṛgaromāṇi … Many other occurrences, but not noted outside of. One might be tempted to emend to ˚rika, were the cases not so numerous.
in evam-ā˚, uncorrected misprint for (evam-)abhiprāyāś, with Calc.]

, adj. (from Skt. abhiprāya with suffix ika; once in Skt. in,, nach Belieben geschehend, beliebig, with karman), (specially, esoterically) intentional, intended: (gambhīrāṇāṃ tathāgatabhāṣitānāṃ … sūtrāntānām) ˚kaṃ tathāgatānām artham avijñāya; ˚ka-nigūḍha-dharma-saṃjñārthavibhāvanatā. See s.v. saṃdhā.
, adj. (= abhi˚ 1; once in Skt. in different mg.,), proud: and (prose; both times v.l. ādhi˚ or adhi˚); (prose, no v.l.); (prose) ˚ka-vyākaraṇa-vacanā; (prose) ˚kaś ca bhavaty ātmotkarṣī.
(nt.; from Skt. abhirūpa, beautiful, with suffix ya; once Lex. in Skt.,), beauty: ˚pya-kāmasya cākāmaṃ vairūpyataḥ.

, f. ˚kī (cf. an-abhisaṃskārikā, and Pali abhisaṃkhārika; records abhi˚, but has ā-while could intend either ā- or a-), characterized by accumulation (of karman; abhisaṃskāra): ābhisaṃskārikī … nirodhasamāpattiḥ; nābhisaṃskārikair buddhā lakṣaṇair lakṣaṇānvitāḥ.

(adj.), ˚kam, adv. (to abhisaṃkṣepa, q.v.), app. in a manner produced by compression, condensation: (so also; abhi˚) = Tib. bsdus pa las gyur pa; but the real meaning of this seemingly technical term escapes me. The next word is abhyavakāśikam (ābhy˚), q.v.
, adj. (from Skt. abhīkṣṇam; cf. Skt. Lex. ābhīkṣṇa, nt.), recurring, repeated, constant: yam ābhikṣṇakaṃ vipratisāram ādīnavadarśanam āgamya …

, recorded only in ger. forms with object paryaṅkam (= Pali pallaṅkam ābhuj-; Skt. seems to have used badhnāti instead, but, record only noun cpds. such as paryaṅka-bandha; BHS also uses forms of bandhati, as paryaṅka bandhitvă (vs); a theory of the orig. mg. in which is not repeated in; for other theories see s.vv. ābhujati, pallaṅka), having assumed a sitting posture with the legs doubled under the buttocks; in prose of all texts except, only paryaṅkam ābhujya:; (here baddhvā, cf. above);;;;;;;;;;, etc.; in vss, ˚kam ābhujiya; ˚kam ābhujitvā; in prose of ˚kam ābhuñjitvā;, also v.l. where ābhujitvā; the latter is a v.l. for text ābhuṃj˚ (=, mss. corrupt); ābhuṃjitvāna mss. at (vs, bad meter).

, m. (derived by, from bhuj bend, as Anbiegung = Anlehnung; an-ā˚, ohne Anlehnung d.h. ohne Rückhalt oder Stützpunkt. Some Pali interpreters also derive from this root, see. Whatever the etymology, the primary mg. in BHS is clearly effort; so some Skt. lexx., = yatna. This also fits at least many Pali occurrences of ābhoga, but in Pali the word needs more study; dict. definitions are all unsatisfactory; it is often bracketed or equated with manasikāra, esp. with cetaso or cittassa,, perhaps as (mental) effort, e.g.), effort, earnest application (directed towards, loc.): = Tib. sgrim pa, ḥjug pa, bzo (gzo) ba, endeavor; setting about; work; śīle ābhogaṃ kṛtvāna, having made effort for (in regard to) morality;; ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ, one must strive for …;;;; sarvābhogavigato 'nābhogadharmatāprāptaḥ kāyavākcittautsukyāpagataḥ, rid of all (interested) effort, arrived at a state of effortless (impassive, see anābhoga) condition, free of bodily, vocal, mental desires (said of the Bodhisattva); in, list of six ‘hindrances’ (āvaraṇa) to samādhi: kausīdya, māna, śāṭhya, auddhatya, anābhoga, satyābhoga; here anābhoga lack of effort has a bad sense, not a good one as in; satyābhoga is obscure (saty-ābhoga, effort directed towards something concretely existing as distinguished from abstract goals? if satya-ābhoga, as cpd., I do not understand what it could mean as a hindrance to samādhi). See anābhoga, sābhoga, both clearly supporting mg. effort.

, adj. and subst. m. or nt. (as m. = abhy˚, q.v.), (an ascetic) living in the open air (one of the 12 dhūta-guṇa): = Tib. bla gab med pa (see);; nt. ˚kam, the practice of living as such an ascetic, (Kyoto ed. abhy˚, but Index also ābhy˚, and ābhy˚) = Tib. mṅon par skabs yod pa (see).
, interj. (= Pali, Pkt. id., once in Jain Skt.,; cf. Skt. ām), yes (giving consent or approval):;; sa kathayaty āmeti.

, m., defined in as = religious longings (lit. thirsts; could the word be connected with Skt. Lex. āma, m., disease? i.e. pathological state?): … mahāsattvasyāmaḥ; āmaḥ, dharmatṛṣṇāḥ;, etc., dharmatṛṣṇā āmaḥ. See s.v. mūdhāma.

, m. (see also nir-āma˚; = Pali id.; defined by vissa-gandha, and cf. sāmagandhā [so read with v.l.] glossed by sa-kuṇapagandhā pūtigandhā), the odor of carrion; (more loosely) stench, evil odor: literally, (vs) (kāye …) kuṣṭhaṃ kilāsaṃ tatha āmagandhaḥ; (after 13 vividhagandhapuṣpāś ca upavāyantu sarvataḥ) mānuṣāṇām [Page100-a] āmagandhāś (em. ˚dhā) ca śīghram antarahāpaya (5 mss. ˚hāpanā or ˚ṇā); fig. of the stench of immorality, opp. of the odor of sanctity, ke āmagandhā manujeṣu brahma, and 11 (after a list of vices) te āmagandhā manujeṣu brahma (corresp. to Pali and). This is the basis of the usually fig. meaning of nirāmagandha.
(m. or nt.; from Skt. ā-math-), agitation, violent stirring, or perhaps concretely eddy, whirlpool: mahaughormy-āmathair nimagnā vateme sattvāḥ …

, in an-āma˚, adj. (neg. Bhvr. to Skt. āmantraṇa, Pali āmantaṇa or ˚na; in Pali āmantanikā is recorded in a concrete, personal application), having no conversation, characterized by not talking with people: of ascetic practices, (ātāpana-paritāpanaiḥ …) anāmantraṇakair (prose).
(only Vedic and very rare; not recorded in MIndic), desires, intends, longs: (vs) eṣo cāham api āmaṃsye (1 sg. fut.; v.l. āmaṃsa) vandituṃ puruṣottamam. But I suspect a corruption.
(formally caus. to Skt. āmārṣṭi, āmṛjati), purifies (a maṇḍalaka, 3, q.v.): bhagavato maṇḍalakam āmārjaya; tayor (gen.) dve te āsanaprajñaptī kṛtau (sic!) dvau maṇḍalakāv āmārjitau.
, m. (= amila, q.v., for which var. āmila occurs), presumably the same kind of cloth called amila: ˚lā(ḥ), n. pl.

, ppp. (MIndic for Skt. āmlāna; cf. Pali milāta = Vedic mlāta), withered; āmilātaṃ (bhavati) saṃmilātaṃ saṃpuṭa(ka)jātaṃ;;;, all prose, in modulations of the same phrase; the corresponding passage has the regular Skt. āmlāna.

, nt. (except for the strange āmiṣā; the BHS word also has its Skt. meanings, as well as those listed here, in which it = Pali āmisa; even in Skt. a few occurrences approach this sphere of use, cf. s.v., Alles worüber man mit Gier herfällt), lit. or orig. (the) flesh (contrasting with dharma, as in Pali with dhamma, the spirit); worldly things, possessions, or enjoyments, as contrasted with religious or spiritual ones (dharma): āmiṣā (! so also) = Tib. zaṅ ziṅ, matter, object, goods; external goods, earthly possessions (contrasted with internal, spiritual gifts); also śa, meat, and zas, food; sāmiṣaḥ, q.v.,, and nirāmiṣaḥ, q.v., (here āmiṣa = Tib. zaṅ ziṅ, only); dual dvandva dharmāmiṣa, spiritual and worldly things, ˚ṣābhyāṃ yathāśaktyā saṃgrāhakaś ca; ˚ṣābhyāṃ dāne 'matsariṇo; atha dharmāmiṣam iti bhagavan kaḥ padārthaḥ; āmiṣam, defined at length in 6—13 as including what leads to longing (tṛṣṇā, 10) and rebirth, away from the religious goal; cf. āmiṣasaṃgraho bhavati na dharmasaṃgraha iti; lokāmiṣasaṃgraho bhavati na dharmasaṃgraha iti; lokāmiṣa-phalābhilāṣiṇo (gen. sg.) vā punaḥ lokāmiṣanimittaṃ tathāgatacaityapūjā; dharmasaṃbhoga āmiṣasaṃbhogo spiritual and worldly enjoyment; in Mahākāśyapa is described as the Lordʼs dharmajo dharmanirmito dharmadāyādo na āmiṣadāyādo, spiritually born, spiritually fashioned spiritual heir, not physical (or worldly) heir (Pali also uses dhamma- and āmisa-dāyāda); āmiṣalolupaḥ puṅgalo … bodhisattvena na sevitavyaḥ; apy oṣitā āmiṣapātracīvare (so prob. divide, see oṣita); āmiṣa-priyāś fond of worldly things; āmiṣa-gurukasya devoted to …; nāmiṣaprakṣiptayā samtatyā, with mental disposition (see saṃtati) not intent on worldly (or material) things; āmiṣa-kiṃcitka, see kiṃcitka; na labhyaṃ bhikṣavas tenāmiṣeṇāmiṣakṛtyaṃ kartum, it is not allowable to pursue enjoyment with this worldly enjoyment (sugar added to food).

, ppp., f. ˚tā, acc. to jewel, in (ratnapratyuptikayā) karṇikayā āmuktayālaṃkṛtaḥ; koṭimūlyayā ratnapratyuptikayā āmuktayā jātaḥ; and see āmuktaka, ˚ikā. I doubt this mg.; in it seems a normal ppp. = Skt. āmukta, ˚ā: adorned with a jewel-set earring fastened on him (cf. also āmuktamālyābharaṇā, with garlands and ornaments fastened on); this is a regular mg. of āmuñcati. In, to be sure, no noun is expressed; the same karṇikā of is however clearly meant; possibly here ratna-pratyuptikayā may be understood as a subst., with specifying ka (): with a jewel-studded thing fastened on.]
, f. ˚ikā (= Skt. āmukta, ppp.), fastened on: tasya ratnakarṇikā karṇe āmuktikā. (Taken by Index as noun, jewel; see s.v. āmukta.) I see no meaning in the suffix ka ().

, adj., (presenting itself) before oneʼs face; present, at hand: mṛtyor mukham ivāmukham (… vaḍabāmukham); āmukhi (m.c. for ˚khe; one ms. ˚kha) sarvi bhaveyu samagrāḥ, may they all be present (to me; āmukhi prob. loc. sg., adverbial, rather than n. pl. with pronominal ending); (vs) māramaṇḍalaraṇasmi āmukhe (loc. abs.), when the battle … is at hand; -saddharmāntardhānim āmukhām upagatāṃ paśyati; (bhayabhairavair) āmukhaiḥ. Cf. the following items, and s.v. poṣadha.
(denom. from prec.), presents, puts before one: śūnyaṃ jagad akhilam āmukhayet.
(n. act. to next), the making present, realization, manifestation: -bodhicittāmukhīkaraṇa-; -samāpatty-āmukhīkaraṇa-tayā (instr. of tā); (cf.); punar-āmukhīkaraṇena.

(see āmukha, and cf. prec.), makes present (regularly in oneself), realizes, manifests: -karoti (buddhadharmān); (dharmamukhāni; cf. also id. 7, 9, etc.); (śilpakarmasthānam); -kṛtya, ger. (-upāyakauśalyam); (bodhipakṣān dharmān);; (Acalām upāsikām; keeping present in his mind); (śūnyatām); (pariśuddhatām).
(= -bhūta, see next), (which have) come to be present to oneʼs mind, realized: (tasya … tisro) gāthā ā˚ ˚ttā jātāḥ, three verses occurred to him, were presented to his mind.

(see āmukha, and cf. prec. and foll. items), becomes present (to oneself, to oneʼs mind), is realized, is manifest: ˚vati (bodhicittam); (prajñāpāramitāvihāra); ˚vanti na ca tāvat tasya te dharmā ā˚ (so both edd., but most mss. abhimukhī-bha˚); (pūrvapraṇidhānapadāny); (samāpattiśatāny); ppp. -bhūto (dīpaṃkarabuddhaśabdo …); -bhūtam (nīlakṛtsnam); (sthavirāṇāṃ vacanam).

, ppp. (cf. prec. items and especially āmukha), situated facing or in the presence of (with acc.): (vs) tathāgataḥ sattva sarvi (acc. pl.) samam āmukhīsthitaḥ, facing (or in the presence of) all creatures at once. (Perhaps in the minds of, but in the sense that he knows their minds.)
, adj. (Skt. amutra with suffix ika), of a future life or other world: aihikaḥ āmutrikaḥ;.
, adj. (ā plus mṛduka, q.v.), rather mild: ˚ko bhaviṣyati.
, nt., touching, enjoyment; only as etymologizing substitute for, and interpretation of, āmiṣa, q.v.: (in definition of āmiṣa) āmiṣam āmṛśam …
, adj., gdve. to next, subject of rejoicing, to be rejoiced over: śuddhāvāsā ca devā aṣṭādaśa āmodanīyāṃ dharmān pratilabhanti (listed in sequel).
(= Pali ˚deti; prob. denom. to āmoda), gratifies: ˚dayitvā (so read, text āmohayitvā).

, (m. or nt.) ˚rye (prose), one of the arts (kalā); from the context (after bārhaspatye and before āsurye) perhaps a philosophic system; v.l. ambhīrye (also ācīrye, asvīrye, but Tib. chuḥi lugs, way, or system, of water indicates that the orig. began ambh- or āmbh-, tho it does not give much further help).
(= Pali Ambatitthaka), n. of a nāga:.

(also ˚likā; = Pali Ambapālī, ˚likā; in Pali and in she was a courtesan), n. of a Licchavi woman, who donated her mango grove to the Buddha:; in Buddha is dwelling at Vaiśālī in this grove, Āmrapālī-vane; her miraculous origin,; in mss. of, e.g., regularly written Amra˚ (semi-MIndic).
, perh. gears up, makes work (a machine): (Tib. sbyar, put together, prepare).
, m. (= Skt. amla˚, and lex. āmla˚), n. of a plant, a kind of sorrel, Rumex vesicarius: = Tib. star bu, acc. to Hippophae rhamnoides, but ‘acc. to a Lex. also a kind of sorrel in India.’

, caus. to ā-mlā (in Skt. only in āmlāna; caus. of mlā in Skt. is mlāpayati), causes to wither: fut. medio-passive (pass. force) āmlāyiṣyase … bodhisattvena, you shall be made to wither by the Bodhisattva (said to Māra).

, m. (in Skt., and usually in Pali, only income, opp. to vyaya expense; rarely in Vedic and Up. something like arrival; see, and son in Pali e.g. udakass' āya-mukham, acc. to comm. = āgamana-maggo; see also āya-dvāra), coming, arrival, esp. coming into existence, origination, source: (vs), replacing āyadvāraṃ, q.v., of prose above, karṣāpaṇāyo … bhoti, saṃbodhicittasya ca yatra āyo, āyo bahū tatra ca śrāvakāṇām; same comparison (vs), āyu and āyo again replacing āyadvāraṃ of prose; āyaḥ = Tib. ḥbuṅ ba (meaning?), or, ḥdu ba, coming together; associated or cpd. with vyaya, (in Skt. income and outlay, but) here origination, coming into being, and passing away (belief in which is a false opinion), āya-vyayadṛṣṭābhiniveśena; nāhaṃ mahāmate lokāyataṃ deśayāmi, na cāyavyayam, kiṃ tu mahāmate anāyavyayaṃ deśayāmi. tatrāyo nāma mahāmate utpādarāśiḥ samūhāgamā, utpadyante (read ˚gamād utpadyate with Tib. acc. to note). tatra vyayo nāma … vināśaḥ. an-āyavyaya ity an-utpādasyaitad adhivacanam; āyaṃ kāryārthanirvṛttiṃ (accs. sg., obj. of paśyate, prec. line), and 4 āyavyaya-parijñānād; sarvāyāśrayaniśrita-vihāra-vihāriṇām (does āya here mean cause, basis, origin?).

, nt. (in Skt. seat, abiding-place, home; the following senses seem hardly, if at all, to occur in Skt., but most of them apparently in Pali), (1) department, field (of art): in śilpāyatana (= Pali sippāy˚), sarvaśilpāyatanehi … kuśo kumāro viśiṣyati, Prince Kuśa excelled in all departments of art; but the same word is also used (2) personally, applying to practitioners of the arts (perhaps as vessels, pātra, of the arts, cf. 3 below): sarve ca kapilavāstavyā śilpāyatanā (as masc.? one ms. ˚nāḥ!), tad yathā lohakārakā etc. (list of artisans), all the artisans of Kapilavastu, such as …; similarly śilpāyatanā (no v.l.), tad yathā lohakārakā etc.; in the same way tīrthyāyatana (vessel of heresy?) is used of heretical teachers yānīmāni … pṛthag loke [Page101-b] tīrthyāyatanāni, tad yathā, Pūraṇaḥ Kāśyapo Māskarī etc. (all persons); Pali has titthāyatana, nt., only as heretical school or doctrine (acc. to harbours of error), or at least, it seems, never clearly of persons (some passages are ambiguous and might be so interpreted); Pali sippāyatana also does not seem to be applied to artisans, but only to crafts; (3) a worthy object (cf. an-āy˚), = Skt. pātra: (api tu Buddhadharmasaṃghe) prasādam utpādaya, eṣa āyatanagataḥ prasāda iti, … this is favor bestowed on a worthy object; (4) stage of ecstasy or trance (four such), see ākāśānantyāyat˚, vijñānānantyāyat˚, ākiṃcanyāyat˚, naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyat˚: listed; also in list of samāpatti, q.v.;; see also s.v. deva; (5) sense; organ of sense (six in number), distinguished as ādhyātmika āy˚ (= Pali ajjhattika āy˚) or as sparśāy˚ (= Pali phassāy˚); likewise object of sense (also six), distinguished as bāhira (= Pali id.) or bāhya āy˚: dvādaśāyatanāni, listed in pairs, each cpd. with āyatanam (cakṣur-āy˚ etc.); the standard list contains six of each category, viz. cakṣus and rūpa, śrotra and śabda, ghrāṇa and gandha, jihvā and rasa, kāya and spraṣṭavya (q.v.), manas and dharma (2); lists each group of six as a (dvandva) cpd. concluded by āyatanāni (with sparśa in lieu of spraṣṭavya); ṣaḍ imāni … sparśāyatanāni, katamāni ṣaṭ, cakṣuḥ sparśāyatanaṃ rūpāṇāṃ darśanāya, etc., including kāya (read kāyaḥ) sparśāy˚ spraṣṭavyānāṃ sparśanāya, manaḥ sparśāy˚ dharmāṇāṃ vijñānāya; ādhyātmikam āy˚ and bāhiram āy˚ (parallel passage in Pali,); ṣaḍ-āyatanam, the six senses (sense-organs and their respective objects, each pair regarded as a unit), one of the steps in the pratītya-samutpāda (= Pali saḷāyatana),;;; etc., cf.,; actions are rooted in them, (vs) iha me karmavidhānā … ṣaḍāyatanamūlā, chinnā drumendramūle (i.e. by attaining Buddhahood); compounded or associated with skandha, q.v., and dhātu (element, q.v.), the total being an expression for states of physical existence, (vs) na skandha āyatana dhātu (better as dvandva cpd.?) vademi buddhaṃ, I do not call … the Buddha; (cited; vs) skandhadhātvāyatanāni (prob. read with skandhāyatanāni, better meter; so also Tib.) dhātavaḥ; skandha-dhātv-āyatanopagānāṃ sarvadharmāṇām; (6) abhibhv-āyatana, see s.v.; (7) kṛtsnāyatana, q.v., s.v. kṛtsna.

, ifc. adj. (āyatana 5 with suffix ika), in dharmāyatanikam, prob. having to do with or based on the ‘sphere’ of dharmas (as objects of manas, see āyatana 5), i.e. ‘objects of ideation’ (s.v. dhamma, cpd. dhammāyatana). In Pali, -āyatanika is recorded only in phassāyatanikā nāma nirayā, and … saggā, and 17—18, hells or heavens based on the ‘contact fields’ or senses (cf. sparśāyatana s.v. āyatana 5), with unpleasant or pleasant sensations respectively.
, adv. (Pali id.; acc. of Skt. āyati, the future, but not recorded there as adv.), in the future: ˚tiṃ saṃbodhim abhisaṃprārthayamānena, or bodhiṃ prārthayamānena.

, nt. (see āya), (1) cause or means (lit. door) of arrival or origin: of rain, jewels, money, flowers, tad yathāpi … vyabhre deve vigatavalāhake nāsti varṣasyāyadvāraṃ, evam eva … alpaśrutasya bodhisattvasyāntikā (read ˚kān) nāsti saddharmavṛṣṭer āyadvāraṃ: tad yathāpi … yatra maṇiratnāyadvāraṃ bhavati, bahūnāṃ tatra karṣāpaṇaśatasahasrāṇām āyadvāraṃ bhavati; evam eva … yatra bodhisattvasyāyadvāraṃ bhavati, bahūnāṃ tatra śrāvakapratyekabuddhaśatasahasrāṇām āyadvāraṃ bhavati (in lines 6, 7, vs, āyo replaces āyadvāraṃ; same comparison, [Page102-a] āyadvāraṃ, replaced in vs by āyu 7, āyo 9); bahūnāṃ puṣpaśatasahasrāṇām āyadvāraṃ bhaviṣyatīti; of dharma, (dve ime … bodhisattvasya) mahatī kuśaladharmāyadvāre (dual); sarvadharmāyadvāra-tayā; others, kalyāṇamitrāyadvārāḥ, having good friends as their origin or cause (agrees with series of nouns ending sarvabuddhadharmapratilambhapariniṣpattayaḥ,); āyadvārārthena ṣaḍāyatanam and (cf. with note: la porte dʼarrivée, la porte de naissance); (2) source of income (cf. Skt. āya, income), substantially = karmānta: udāreṣu ca karmānteṣv adhimukto bhavati, na parīttāyadvāreṣu; perhaps in this sense saṃghāyadvāraharaṇam, depriving the assembly (of monks) of sources of income (? in a list of sins; Tib. is literal and not helpful).
(nt., = Pali id., to Skt. and Pali āyācati), supplication (of a deity): āyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante; ˚nena.

(to Skt. āyācati, cf. Skt. yācñā), entreaty: (prose) -parisamāpty-āyācñayā, with entreaty to complete … Crit. app. suggests em. to ˚pti-yācñayā, but the formation seems quite possible (to āyācati as yācñā to yācati).
, m., guard or attendant on a journey: kimarthaṃ vayam ˚kāṇāṃ bhṛtim anuprayacchāmaḥ.
, ppp. (of Skt. āyāpayati, not in this mg.), reared, brought up: (tvaṃ mayā …) svahastabalenāyāpitaḥ poṣitaḥ saṃvardhitaḥ.
, m., ˚saḥ, read ācāmaḥ with Tib. (letter from) and same passage, cf. etc.]

(?), n. of a Bodhisattva:. Uncertain reading; initial in saṃdhi with preceding -a, permitting analysis as Ayudhi˚, which seems scarcely possible; perhaps the long ā is an error or misprint, and we should understand Yudhiṣṭhira.
, adj. ifc. (from āyus with suffix ika), aged …: (prose) (jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ …) anekavarṣaśatasahasrāyuṣikaḥ.

, i.e. Skt. āyuṣman, functions like Pali āvuso (see āvusa and āyuṣmaṃvāda), and like it (see s.v.) may be {{adressed->addressed||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} to more than one person, sirs (usually to equals or inferiors): (prose) (te bhikṣū … kumbhakārasya mātāpitarau etad uvāca), yatra āyuṣmaṃ bhikṣū (n. pl., so read with mss., wrongly em. bhikṣūṇāṃ) … tṛṇā na saṃbhuṇanti …
(m.; = Pali āvusovāda,; cf. āyuṣmaṃ), address using the term āyuṣmaṃ (āyuṣman): (mā bhikṣavo …) tathāgataṃ āyuṣmaṃvādena samudācaratha (in corresponding passage āyuṣmadvādena, regular Skt.).

(Pali id.), effort, striving, chiefly in neg. anāyūha (also anāvyūha), q.v. for discussion of mg.; cf. also āyūhati: āyūhaniryūha-vigata (= anāyūhāniryūha) ˚tam (traidhātukam); ˚tāḥ (sarvadharmāḥ); in āyūha-sarvadharma-vimāna-pratiṣṭhānāṃ (bodhisattvānāṃ), prob. error for anāyūha-.

(= Pali id.), cf. (an)āyūha, exerts oneself, strives (for, acc.): (bodhisattvavimokṣam; similarly in the rest);;; (in all these followed by corresp. form of niryūhati, q.v.); ˚hantī, followed by viyūhantī; passive, āyūhyamānaṃ nāyūhyate, niryūhyamānaṃ na niryūhyate, ata etasmāt kāraṇān … sarvadharmā āyūhaniryūhavigatāḥ, [Page102-b] being striven after it is not attained (or [successfully] striven after), being renounced it is not got rid of; that is why all states of existence are without either acquisition or riddance (, neither taking birth nor … going out).

, m. (= Pali id.; in sense 1 Skt. Lex., and acc. to once in, but acc. to bhramarāyoga there means Bienenschwarm), (1) practice (of), application (to), with loc. or as posterior in cpd.: sukhallikāyoga, addiction to pleasures (otherwise ˚kānuyoga, which alone seems to be known in Pali), see s.v. sukhallikā,;; adhicitte ca āyoga(ḥ) (= Pali, same text); (2) in (prose) (dhanikaḥ) syād āyogaprayoga-kṛṣi-vaṇijya-prabhūtaś ca bhavet, and in corresponding vs prayoga āyoga …; here both āyoga and prayoga apparently mean different kinds of business activity; acc. to Tib. it seems that āyoga = ḥdu ba, accumulation (of wealth), prayoga = ḥphel ba, increase (qy: by usury?), but acc. to also accumulation, collection, excess.

, nt., the hither or nearer side or part, in contrast to pāra: = Tib. tshu rol, this side ( pāraṃ); (kasyacid dharmasyotpādaṃ vā nirodhaṃ vā …) āraṃ vā pāraṃ vopalabhate. (Cf. AMg. āra, nt., this world, this life, this existence. Doubtless the stem from which is derived the Skt. adverb ārāt near, see s.v. ārād-upakāraka.)

, m.:, text ārakṣān sthāpayati sma, he establishes guards. But v.l. rakṣā; read either this or ārakṣāṃ; in any case the stem is fem. (in -ā); cf. ārakṣāṃ prakarotha. In ms. ārakṣāṇi, ed. ārakṣyāṇi; read arakṣyāṇi, see arakṣya.]

, m. or nt. (associated with ārāgayati, q.v.; root raj, rañj, cf. Skt. raṅga etc.), acquisition, attainment: (prose) sarvakuśalamūladharmāraṅgottāraṇāya, to the bringing over into acquisition of … Tib. brtsams, accomplishment.
, m. (Skt. id., forest dweller, not in technical sense; = Pali āraññaka, also ara˚ in both BHS and Pali), dwelling in the forest, one of the dhūtaguṇa:;;;.
, adv. (= Skt. ārāt), at a distance, afar (from, with gen.): (vs) tasya sarvi sugatā na durlabhā, tasya sarvi jinaputra nārataḥ.

, f., n. of one of the ‘armies’ (senā) of Māra: (vs) kāmā te prathamā senā dvitīyā ārati vuccati. The meter is indifferent as to a- or ā- initially, and in the same vs has Arati, q.v. It is hard to be sure what meaning was attributed to the word. (mécontentement) and Tib. (mi dgaḥ ba) understand as a-(neg.)-rati.

, ger., postpos. with acc. (= Pali ārabbha), referring to, having to do with: (taṃ varaprabhaṃ bodhisattvam) ārabhya … dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayām āsa (practically = revealed to the bodhisattva Varaprabha); samyaksaṃbodhim ārabhya … bodhisattvayānam eva samādāpayati;; (prose) sattvān ārabhya mahākaruṇām avakrāmayati sma (= sattveṣu ca mahākaruṇām avakrāmati sma); … śrotuṃ imam eva mārakaraṇḍaṃ nigamam ārabhya (about); … pṛccheyaṃ dṛṣtadhārmikaṃ artham ārabhya utāho sāṃparāyikaṃ; pañca kāmaguṇān ārabhya; (aniyataṃ) rāśim ārabhya; yaśodaṃ śreṣṭhiputraṃ ārabhya imam udānam udānaye;; sthaviropaguptam ārabhya; bhikṣuṇyāḥ [Page103-a] pūrvanivāsam ārabhya bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma (repetitions below); (vs) … tad brūhi kam ārabhyeti bhāṣase; yathāvadbhāvikatāṃ dharmāṇām ārabhya yā bhūtatā; Saṃthakātyāyanam ārabhya; hīnayāna-niḥsṛtiṃ cārabhya mahāyāna-niḥsṛtiṃ vā; etc.

, nt. (= Pali ārammaṇa; in mg. 1 = Skt. ālambana; in BHS this, q.v., is also used in mg. 3), (1) basis, support, point dʼappui; basis, reason, (logical) ground; in Bhvr. cpds., having … as basis, based on …: (see s.v. āśravaṇa); -vividha-hetu-kāraṇa-nidarśanārambaṇa-niruktyupāyakauśalyair; yāṃ ca … tathāgataḥ … vācaṃ bhāṣata ātmopadarśanena (add with vā paropadarśanena) vātmārambaṇena vā parārambaṇena vā …, either on his own authority () or that of others, or on the basis of (presentation of) himself (in visible form) or of others (so essentially; perhaps more exactly, on the basis of giving an account, a description, sc. of himself, by himself or by others); vividhair ārambaṇair, with various bases or authorities; tad ārambaṇaṃ kṛtvā, probably making that my reason or basis; tathāgatārambaṇa-manaskārakuśalamūlāni, roots of merit (due to) attentiveness based upon the Tathāgata; (dhyānagocarāṇāṃ) ca samāpattyārambaṇānāṃ laukikasamādhīnām; mahantānāṃ varṇānām ārambaṇam … (16) bhūtānāṃ ca varṇānām ārambaṇam anuprāpnuvanti (Bodhisattvas), apparently basis of great castes … and of bygone castes* (so, but he disclaims understanding what is meant); -bodhy-ārambaṇa- (1st ed. misprinted; corr. 2d ed.) -kuśalamūla-; and ārambaṇīkṛtya, making a basis, object of attention (with acc.); in ārambaṇena = ālambanapratyayena (cf.; Pali ārammaṇapaccaya), the third of the four pratyaya, q.v.; (2) physical basis, location (= Skt. viṣaya): yasmin yasminn adhvani (time, i.e. present, past, or future) yasmin yasminn ārambaṇe (cosmic location, of a Tathāgata) … tathāgataṃ draṣṭum ākāṅkṣāmi; ābhāsam agamann ekasminn ārambaṇe yathā caikasminn ārambaṇe tathāśeṣasarvārambaṇeṣu, location(s), of the palatial structures presided over by Maitreya; (3) like Pali ārammaṇa, also = Skt. viṣaya in sense of sense-object, of which in Pali there are six (the 6th being dhamma, object of manas); cakṣurindriyādhipateyā rūpārambaṇa-prativijñaptiḥ, recognition of the sense-object form, dependent on the sense-organ eye (sight);, read with mss. ārambaṇārambhaṇacittaṃ hetuno parikarmenti, … the thought as it grasps the sense-objects (here perhaps more particularly the objects of the manas, ideas, to which Pali ārammaṇa is sometimes restrictedly applied). -*() Better, basis of great and true renown, or qualities, or (physical) appearance?
